title: Functions
summary: Learn how to reuse code using functions.

steps.title: What is a Function?
steps.markdownContent: A function is a named block of reusable instructions. It helps avoid repeating code and keeps your program organized.

steps.title: Calling Functions
steps.markdownContent: You use a function by calling its name followed by parentheses: `blink();`. Sometimes you pass parameters, like `digitalWrite(13, HIGH);`.

steps.title: Return Values
steps.markdownContent: Some functions give back a result (like `digitalRead()`). If a function doesn't give anything back, it uses the keyword `void`.

steps.title: Execution Speed Visualizer
steps.markdownContent: Watch how calling a function executes its block of code.

steps.title: Knowledge Check
steps.markdownContent: Test what you learned about functions.

questions.question: What is a function?
options: A named block of reusable instructions
questions.explanation: Functions bundle instructions so they can be reused easily.

questions.question: What does `void` mean?
questions.explanation: Void indicates that the function performs an action but doesn't return a data value.

questions.question: What are the values passed inside the parentheses called?
questions.explanation: Parameters (or arguments) provide data to the function.
